label: Affine Epipolar Geometry
notes: This chapter covers the affine two-view case across printed pages 344 to 362. When the camera centre recedes to infinity, projection becomes parallel, the epipoles move to infinity, and the dense projective machinery simplifies to linear algebra in four measured image coordinates. Set up the contrast with the projective pencil from the start.

label: The Affine Camera
notes: Emphasise that the affine camera is defined by replacing the bottom row of the projection matrix with zero, zero, zero, one. This kills the perspective division, so image coordinates become linear in world coordinates. Stress that it is an excellent model for distant, shallow scenes viewed through long lenses where depth variation is small.

label: Parallel Projection Limit
notes: Walk through the diagram showing how converging perspective rays straighten into a parallel bundle as the centre retreats. This is the geometric heart of the chapter: parallel rays are what send the epipole to infinity. Anchor the intuition that affine geometry is the limit of perspective for a far, flat object.

label: Parallel Epipolar Lines
notes: Contrast the two pencils directly using the side-by-side figure. In the projective case lines converge to a finite epipole; in the affine case the epipole is at infinity so every epipolar line in an image is parallel, sharing one normal direction. This is the single most recognisable signature of an affine pair.

label: The Affine Fundamental Matrix
notes: Present the sparse form of F_A with only four structural nonzero entries plus the scalar e. Explain that the upper two by two block is zero, which forces the epipoles to infinity. The correspondence constraint reduces to one linear equation in x prime, y prime, x, y, the fact that drives every later algorithm.

label: Degrees of Freedom and Epipoles
notes: Count the parameters: five entries up to scale gives four degrees of freedom, against seven for the general fundamental matrix. Show that the right and left epipoles are ideal points read directly off the entries, and that F_A is automatically rank two. Tie the zero block to the parallel-line property established earlier.

label: Estimation as Hyperplane Fitting
notes: Reframe estimation geometrically: each correspondence is a point in four-dimensional measurement space, and the affine epipolar equation says all of them lie on a hyperplane. Fitting F_A is fitting that hyperplane. The normal vector gives a, b, c, d and the offset gives e. This is the chapter's key algorithmic simplification.

label: The Gold Standard Is Closed Form
notes: Make the punchline explicit: because the affine reprojection error is exactly quadratic, the Gold Standard estimate has no iterative inner loop. Centre the data, take the SVD, and read the smallest singular vector as the hyperplane normal. Total least squares orthogonal regression delivers the maximum likelihood estimate directly.

label: Parallax and the Minimal Case
notes: Use the four-point story to show where the line direction comes from. Three coplanar points fix a plane-induced affine transfer; the fourth point's parallax, its departure from that transfer, sets the epipolar direction. Warn that as relief tends to zero parallax vanishes and the estimate becomes ill-conditioned, a planar degeneracy.

label: Exact Affine Triangulation
notes: Explain that affine Sampson correction is exact, not first order. Since the constraint is a genuine hyperplane, the optimal corrected correspondence is the orthogonal projection of the four measured coordinates onto it. The corrected pair satisfies the epipolar equation exactly and feeds directly into affine triangulation. Contrast this with the projective approximation.

label: Affine Reconstruction and Bas-Relief
notes: Cover the two structural results. Two affine views reconstruct the scene up to a three-dimensional affine transformation once a basis of four non-coplanar points is fixed; ratios along parallel lines survive. But the bas-relief ambiguity means the product of depth and turn is fixed while neither factor is, so depth and rotation magnitude cannot be separated.

label: Synthesis
notes: Close by collecting the through-line. The affine camera linearises projection, the fundamental matrix turns sparse and rank two, estimation becomes closed-form hyperplane fitting, triangulation becomes an exact projection, and reconstruction is affine with a residual bas-relief ambiguity. Send students to the notebook to verify the zero pattern and SVD residuals on synthetic data.
